content: The Tatuaje brand was created by Pete Johnson, the owner of Tatuaje Cigars, in close collaboration with José Pepin Garcia. The cigars are manufactured at the El Rey de los Habanos factory in Miami, Florida, and at Tabacalera Cubana S.A. (TACUBA) in Estelí, Nicaragua. The name Tatuaje translates to tattoo in Spanish, reflecting Pete Johnson's personal tattoos. The brand was developed through a close partnership between Pete Johnson and Don Pepin Garcia, with the goal of achieving a specific blend that Pete envisioned. Tatuaje was the first brand that Don Pepin Garcia created independently. The initial Tatuaje cigars were released in 2003. In October 2004, the Tatuaje Cabinet Especiales received a rating of 90 in Cigar Aficionado magazine, and the brand has continued to receive high ratings since then. Awards and Recognition The Tatuaje Cabinet Especiales was named one of the 25 Best Cigars of 2004 by Cigar Aficionado magazine and ranked 4th in the 25 Best Cigars of 2005. The Tatuaje Cabinet Noella was ranked 9th in the 25 Best Cigars of 2006 and received a rating of 92. The Tatuaje brand was named the 2006 Cigar of the Year by Leaf and Ale. Tatuaje cigars have consistently received high ratings in Cigar Aficionado magazine and Cigar Insider Online. The Tatuaje J21 Reserva was highlighted in the August 2007 print issue of Maxim Magazine. Description Tatuaje cigars are full-bodied but vary in strength. They are all Nicaraguan puros, meaning they are made entirely of tobacco grown in Nicaragua. The brand includes four ranges of regular production cigars, along with several limited-release vitolas (specific sizes) made exclusively for certain retailers. Regular Production Lines Tatuaje Cabinet This range includes six vitolas, though seven are listed, with the Petit being a unique size. The cigars feature a simple brown band with white lettering. The Cabinet range uses a Corojo 99 viso wrapper, with lighter-colored wrappers selected for the Especiales. The filler blends vary, offering a spectrum of strength from the refined mellowness of the Especiales to the near-Cuban strength of the Cazadores. Notably, the initials of the first six vitolas spell out the name of Pete Johnson's dog, Hunter. Tatuaje Reserva This range includes three vitolas, with varying filler blends. The wrapper is a Nicaraguan viso, except for the J21, which uses a ligero leaf. These cigars feature a second black band with Reserva and the frontmark in gold lettering. Tatuaje RC This range consists of two figurado vitolas. These medium-bodied cigars start strong and mellow gradually. The band is tri-colored with red, white, and blue stripes, and each cigar is foil-wrapped from the head to the mid-section, reminiscent of old Cuban-style foil-wrapped figurados. The numbers in the vitola name represent the length in millimeters. Tatuaje Cojonu This range includes three full-bodied vitolas. Starting in August 2006, the wrapper was changed from a viso to a ligero wrapper. In addition to the regular Tatuaje band, these cigars have a second gold band with the year of the vitola's introduction in black. The Gran Cojonu, however, is bandless and features a shag (untrimmed) foot. The year in the model name corresponds to the year of introduction, such as the Cojonu 2003, which debuted in 2003. A new Cojonu model is planned for release every three years. Series P This range is a medium-filler cigar (60% medium filler, 40% long filler). It is medium-bodied, a Nicaraguan puro, and uses the same filler blend as the Havana VI. It is manufactured at TACUBA in Estelí, Nicaragua, with a Nicaraguan Habano wrapper and binder. Nuevitas Jibaro Although not part of the Tatuaje line, this cigar was created by Pete Johnson. Unlike most of Pete's cigars, Pepin Garcia was not involved in its creation or production. These cigars were made by Pedro Martin's old Tropical Tobacco factory (now Tabacalera Tropical) in Estelí, Nicaragua. The design was inspired by a custom-rolled Cuban Cohiba and featured a very strong blend. Pete Johnson discontinued production rather than move it to another factory. The cigars were unbanded, had an unfinished foot, and were limited to two figurado vitolas: No. 1 (5 x 54) and No. 2 (6 x 52). Special Productions Bombazos (4 x 46): Produced for Fumare Cigar in Reno, Nevada, featuring a strong, spicy blend. El Cohete (4 x 50): Produced for Tower Cigars, packed in numbered, dated, and signed cabinets of 25. Only 50 cabinets were made, and the cigars were manufactured in Pepin Garcia's Miami factory. La Maravilla (5 5/8 x 46): Produced for Leaf and Ale, featuring an aged viso wrapper that covers the foot of the cigar, similar to the Gran Cojonu. These cigars are foil-wrapped as part of a unique fermentation process, sealing in flavors during aging, akin to how some Cuban cigars are aged in burlap. Other Tatuaje Cigars In November 2006, a special production of Tatuaje Noellas Reservas was released to Tatuaje retailers. The Thermonuclear, a Triple Ligero blend, was an experimental cigar not generally offered for sale due to its extreme strength, as the name suggests.
